item.title: Two economists, a 30 s video podcast

turns.text: Use the full film pipeline: a 30-second short film styled as a video podcast, with both hosts on screen speaking their lines at microphones in a cosy studio. Maya, a Keynesian economist, argues that in a recession the government should spend to restore demand; Leo, an Austrian-school economist, argues that spending and cheap money cause the boom-and-bust and the economy should be left to correct itself. Each gets two short lines, ending on a friendly disagreement. Live-action look, 16:9, for YouTube, general audience.

item.tests: Tests whether a system can turn a story brief with two named characters and four spoken lines into a 30-second film: characters that persist across shots, audible dialogue that carries the argument, and a staged studio.

answer_sheet.Look: Live-action look, a cosy podcast studio with microphones; your call on the rest.

must_haves: Two hosts, a woman and a man, are on screen at microphones in a cosy studio with a live-action look, not animation.

Each host is heard speaking two short lines: Maya argues the government should spend in a recession to restore demand; Leo argues spending and cheap money cause boom and bust and the economy should correct itself.
The lines are audible speech, not only music or silence.
The two hosts stay the same people across the shots.
It ends on a friendly disagreement between them.

stages.text:
Coffee, Yes; Stimulus, No
kind: short
style: Live-action video podcast for YouTube, 16:9; natural textures, warm studio lighting, and a gentle camera push that keeps both hosts on screen.
In Cedar Studio, warm lamplight falls across a walnut table. Maya sits on the left behind Maya’s microphone; Leo sits on the right behind Leo’s microphone. A bookshelf and soft amber curtains fill the background. Both hosts remain visible in a wide shot. On-screen labels identify Maya as “Keynesian economist” and Leo as “Austrian-school economist.”

Maya leans toward Maya’s microphone. “In a recession, government should spend to restore demand and get people working.”

Leo raises an open hand beside Leo’s microphone. “But spending and cheap money fuel the boom that leads to the bust.”

The camera eases closer, keeping both hosts and both microphones in frame. Maya tilts Maya’s coffee mug toward Leo and smiles. “Then we disagree on stimulus, not on having another coffee.”

Leo lifts Leo’s coffee mug toward Maya’s coffee mug, smiling back. “Coffee, yes; stimulus, no—let the economy correct itself.”

items.prompt: A 30-second short film styled as a video podcast, with both hosts on screen speaking their lines at microphones in a cosy studio; live-action look, 16:9, for YouTube, general audience. Generate picture, animation, dialogue and studio sound together at 480p in one continuous shot. 0–3 s: Establish an eye-level medium-wide two-shot. Maya sits left, a woman in her thirties with dark shoulder-length curls and a rust cardigan; Leo sits right, a man in his thirties with short brown hair and a navy sweater. Two black boom microphones face them across a wooden table with two plain ceramic coffee mugs. Warm lamps, soft acoustic panels and a small plant create a cosy studio with natural textures. Begin a gentle camera push, keeping both faces, microphones and hands visible throughout. Hear quiet room tone. Maya has a calm, warm, midrange adult English-speaking voice; Leo has a relaxed, lightly gravelly adult English-speaking voice. 3–9 s: Maya leans toward her microphone, opens one palm and says exactly: "In a recession, government should spend to restore demand." Leo listens. 9–17 s: Leo gently shakes his head and says exactly: "Spending and cheap money cause boom and bust. Let the economy correct itself." Maya listens thoughtfully. 17–23 s: Maya smiles, gestures toward the coffee mugs and says exactly: "I still favor stimulus, but coffee together?" 23–29 s: Leo smiles back, lifts his mug slightly and says exactly: "Coffee, yes. Stimulus, no. Friends can disagree." 29–30 s: Hold both hosts smiling across the table, still amicably unconvinced. No other text, no cuts, no music, no subtitles.
